title: The Essayes or Counsels, Civill and Morall

access.edition_or_version: The Essayes or Counsels, Civill and Morall, ed. Michael Kiernan (Clarendon Press, 1985)

mechanics.premise: Short counsels on public and private life, testing a topic from several angles.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Sententious and compressed; an observation is distilled into a memorable maxim that carries a general truth.
mechanics.point_of_view: Impersonal adviser; the 'I' is largely absent.
mechanics.structure: Brief essays each turning one topic over by weighing arguments against one another.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Aphoristic close, balanced antithesis, metaphor drawn from law, nature and craft; plainness alternating with epigram.
mechanics.imagery: Concrete figuration used to fix an abstraction in memory.
mechanics.critical_reception: Milestone of the English essay and of aphoristic prose; noted by critics as a Montaigne-influenced but distinct form.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Aphorism piled on aphorism without development becomes a quotation list; impersonality tips into tone-detached.
